Done — one execution, passed on the first run.

**What the script does** (`out/T5/solution.py`):
- Loads both base shards, pairs adapter tensors by stripping the `base_model.model.` PEFT prefix, and merges `W += (alpha/r) * B @ A` in float32 (`fan_in_fan_out=false`, so no transpose), asserting the config flag.
- Enforces all four required checks (32 pairs, no `lora_` names, q_proj still `[2048, 2048]`, 114 tensors) plus a key-set match against the base, all before writing.
- Re-shards greedily at 512 MiB of tensor data in base-index key order, writes `model-000NN-of-00010.safetensors` and an index with `weight_map` and `total_size`.

**Result:** 10 shards, 114 tensors, `total_size=5119148032`. Shard tensor data is ≤ 512 MiB everywhere (file sizes run a few hundred bytes over only because of the safetensors header). `lm_head.weight` landed alone in shard 1; `model.embed_tokens.weight` shares shard 2 with one small tensor — at 412 MB it is below the 512 MiB budget, so the "oversized tensor alone" rule described in TASK.md never triggers and packing order decides. I flagged that discrepancy in the report, along with the fact that the reference's shard-naming and key-ordering conventions aren't specified.
